bounds: The watch is TWO NON-RECURSIVE directory watches per armed workspace (<ws>/.mpd/team for the index, <ws>/.mpd/team/teams for the records). Linux inotify has no recursive mode, so this is the portable shape, not a limitation that was worked around.

Subscribing CREATES those directories (a watch cannot be armed on a path that does not exist), so a surface that subscribes may create empty <workspace>/.mpd/team/teams/. Without it the FIRST record of a fresh session — written by an approval, possibly in another process — would be invisible to every subscriber.

On a network filesystem, or a kernel whose inotify watch limit is exhausted, the watch degrades exactly as an unwritable workspace does: in-process notifications only, ONE bounded log line. Neither condition was reproduced here (they are machine-dependent); the refusal path was exercised with (a) an injected throwing factory and (b) a real EEXIST/ENOTDIR refusal in a mounted boot.

The feed follows the TEAM RECORD and the TEAMS INDEX. The sidecar files (staged plan, contracts, hold, mailbox) are deliberately NOT published: the contract's §3.1 enumerates records + index, and widening it would change an interface two other lanes are being written against.
revision is PER PROCESS and per workspace. Two processes serving one workspace count their own windows; the number is a change detector between a client and its own server, not a global sequence.

The window is FIXED at 50 ms (never extended by a late arrival), so a continuously busy team is notified once per 50 ms window instead of postponing its own notification. Measured worst case on the wire: 50 ms write-to-frame.

The keep-alive is a 15 s `: ping`, CAPTURED rather than asserted (repair R-S2): a 22013 ms raw `curl -i -N` whose 269 B are in after-keepalive-body.txt carries the head block, `retry: 1000`, `event: hello`, then `: ping` — with no other frame over the whole window; the live timeline (after-keepalive-sse.txt) puts the comment at +15006 ms after the connect frame and counts 0 change frames in between. A client that disconnects leaves no timer and no listener (asserted in an arm).

The SSE handler flushes the head explicitly (`flushHeaders`) and sets `x-accel-buffering: no` as well as `cache-control: no-store, no-transform`; the host's own gzip filter already skips `text/event-stream`, so no compression layer is in the path — the 50 ms measurement was taken through the real host server. The head is CAPTURED verbatim in after-keepalive-headers.txt (all four headers present); the same capture shows the host adding `Date` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and curl de-chunks the body transparently.
notes: This driver MUST run with `node`, not bun: `dshAppSpec` spawns the harness app with `process.execPath`, and a bun-hosted driver makes the harness app die (bun tempdir EROFS, or a V8-symbol load failure).

`state-parity.ts` is the MIRROR IMAGE and must run with `bun`: it imports the HEAD copy of `src/**` verbatim, whose specifiers are the committed extensionless ones, and node's ESM resolver refuses them (MEASURED: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … /src-at-head/team-store`).

EVERY `sse-boot.ts` PHASE NOW ENDS WITH A CREDENTIAL SWEEP (`redactEvidenceLogs`): the harness prints `dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=…` into the boot log the driver opened, so the logs are redacted and re-read before the phase returns. `--phase sweep` runs the sweep alone and is idempotent — the repaired lane reports `re-read clean: true`.

The install needs XDG_RUNTIME_DIR pointed INSIDE the sandbox: pnpm puts its store operation lock at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pnpm-store-operation-locks-<uid>, and /run/user/<uid> is mounted READ-ONLY inside a workspace-write file sandbox (ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_OPEN_OPERATION_LOCK).

Arming a fresh workspace must CREATE both directories BEFORE arming either watch: creating teams/ inside a watched team root is observed by that watch and was measured as a `hello` frame carrying rev:1 on a workspace that had never been written to.
